feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. It is well written overall, but it would be stronger with tighter structure, fewer repeated themes, and more consistently quantified impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”  
- Good credibility and scale signals: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms add substance.  
- Writing is polished and professional, with no obvious misspellings; tone is consistent and appropriately executive.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Recent Projects” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve focus and save space.  
- Add more outcome-based metrics beyond scope/activity. Several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more results (growth %, efficiency gains, engagement improvements, cost savings) would increase impact.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation and bullet formatting are inconsistent across sections; “English (Native)” / “French (A2/Learning)” would read more cleanly as “Native” / “A2 (learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent NACo experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “Senior digital leader” with a more specific positioning tied to public-sector digital transformation and communications systems.
- Add one proof point from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Tighten the list of responsibilities to avoid sounding like a skills inventory; group related areas.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector web ecosystems, governance models and content operations. Led enterprise website transformation for a 10,000+ page Drupal platform serving 3.5M annual page views, while building analytics, editorial and multimedia systems that improve publishing quality, discovery and audience engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” repeats ideas already covered in Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- The current opening closely mirrors the subtitle and skills sections; use the intro for positioning plus 1–2 standout proof points.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating detailed skill categories.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Recast as broader, executive-level competencies: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and content operations • Analytics, reporting, and performance optimization • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and systems integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style by replacing “&” with “and” for consistency across the CV.
- Consider changing “Multi-channel communications operations” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” to better reflect seniority.
- Consider shortening “AI-enabled search and content experiences” to “AI-enabled search and content discovery” for clearer meaning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially duplicates the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid tool-specific phrasing.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is already reinforced in Work Experience and Technical + IT, so avoid expanding it further here.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently reads like a repeat of the recent consulting and NACo experience rather than a distinct footer highlight. Tightening phrasing and standardizing style will improve scanability and impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, outcome-oriented sentence.
- Standardize parallel structure: start each project with a strong verb and use consistent punctuation/capitalization.
- Replace “10×20-foot” with “10 x 20-foot” for CV style consistency; consider “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” once, not repeatedly.
- Emphasize differentiators not already obvious elsewhere, e.g., legislative search, interactive conference display, modular campaign architecture.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current freelance and NACo bullets; reframe as “selected projects” with unique angles or remove the weakest duplicate.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily; vary verbs to avoid sameness.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads broad and overlaps with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten it around strategic scope, technical ownership, and 1–2 concrete outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvement, and cross-channel content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4 impact-focused bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one line about improving coordination and publishing efficiency.
- Rephrase for ownership and outcomes: “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular content components, and member toolkits to support scalable storytelling and campaign launches.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, workflow time reduced, publishing speed improved, search success/engagement gains, or stakeholder teams enabled.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects footer; keep this entry high-level and let the footer hold the technical detail.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement echo the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize what is new in this consulting engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening emphasized enterprise ownership and if channel-management bullets added clearer outcomes rather than broad reach statements.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opener with: “Directed enterprise digital communications for NACo, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget strategy across a multi-platform public-sector communications operation.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen outcomes on channels: quantify email/social performance if possible (growth, engagement, CTR, list size, campaign results), not just audience size.
- Combine governance/analytics into one results-focused bullet: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery while formalizing publishing standards and cross-department workflows to improve decision-making and operational consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the earlier NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and systems built.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer projects; keep the CV item at capability-and-impact level, not project-detail level.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth at this stage.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets to emphasize scope and outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show ownership and growth: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Improved editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” is very close to the Director role’s channel-overview language.
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier role and footer project; keep the focus here on scaling/operationalizing it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector digital communications
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Stakeholder-focused digital communications” if you want a broader, more senior tone.
- If space allows elsewhere, move “advocacy” emphasis into project/work bullets where outcomes are clearer, and keep this skills block more evergreen.
- Keep each line noun-based and parallel; avoid mixing leadership terms with execution terms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with editorial planning language in the 2018–2022 role.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent work: Drupal-led modernization, integrations/automation, and AI search.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the list with a tighter, higher-signal version: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- De-emphasize older or lower-value terms: remove “jQuery” unless required by target roles; it dates the profile.
- Lead with Drupal/CMS modernization since that is most supported by recent experience and projects.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Drupal modernization for large public-facing sites” or “AI-enabled search and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and more strategic, with detailed tools left below.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating exact phrasing if possible.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. As a topline skills item, it should emphasize strategic analytics leadership and outcomes, not just repeat platforms.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy and reporting infrastructure • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership dashboards • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Tighten wording: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive dashboards” or “Leadership dashboards” for clearer value.
- Group tools together once, then lead with higher-level strengths so this reads as senior-level, not analyst-level.
- If you can support it elsewhere, add impact language such as “decision-ready reporting” or “insight generation for web modernization and campaign optimization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list across sections; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave full tool detail to Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Make it more senior, operational, and tied to recent leadership-level delivery rather than hands-on task lists.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools/tasks to capability + scope, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- If space allows, add scale/ownership language: “enterprise livestream operations” or “studio and event production leadership.”
- Consider replacing “virtual event production” with “hybrid event delivery” to avoid repeating near-synonyms.
- Optional tighter heading/content pairing: keep heading, but make bullets noun-based and parallel.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” skew tactical relative to the seniority of recent roles unless balanced with leadership/ownership language.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is the strongest and most recent platform, give it clearer priority.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider signaling depth: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier instead of just names: “CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project; it feels less central than the enterprise platforms above.
- If you want more impact, tie Drupal to scale elsewhere rather than here; keep this line concise and let work experience carry the metrics.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” under Topline Skills.
- Avoid repeating CMS modernization here if it already appears in Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and tools that support recent, higher-impact work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • jQuery • API and third-party integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions (CI/CD)
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; it feels dated and adds no value.
- If accurate, add one impact-oriented qualifier in the section intro or adjacent summary, e.g., “used to support Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, automation, and lightweight serverless tooling.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; keep the fuller detail here and shorten/remove the duplicate there.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may overlap with GitHub Actions/Cloudflare Workers unless each section has a distinct purpose.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more category-led.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as grouped systems, not a flat list: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Put the strongest/recently relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.
- If space allows, add light context tied to impact: “used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and process automation.”
- Consider dropping one lower-value collaboration tool if you need concision; Slack/Teams are more standard than differentiating.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are adjacent in meaning; listing all four may feel padded unless each was meaningfully used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for this profile, but the line is too bare to add much value on its own. It should signal level of use and align with the strong email/program leadership already shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: Enterprise email campaign delivery, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, and member communications
- If space allows, prioritize by depth/relevance: Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and NACo bullets about newsletters; avoid repeating generic email-management claims elsewhere unless you add specifics like segmentation, automation, or platform migration.
- If you haven’t used Dynamics 365 hands-on, don’t lead with it; ordering should reflect actual proficiency and recency.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is mostly a keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Tighten it to emphasize analytics infrastructure and optimization methods most supported by recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics & Optimization
- Replace with: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • Experimentation
- Swap “A/B testing” for “Experimentation” unless you can point to a specific testing program or result in recent roles.
- Swap “Dashboarding” for “KPI reporting” or “Executive dashboards” to sound more outcome-oriented and less generic.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider trimming one version or making this one tools-only and the other outcomes-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role; avoid repeating the full stack elsewhere unless needed for ATS.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like a setup role rather than showing concrete contributions. Tighten it around team-building, platform work, and recurring multimedia outputs, with metrics if you can add them.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and scope: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Split key contributions into sharper outcomes: website refresh, livestream production, weekly video series, and informal supervision/mentoring.
- Add measurable detail where possible: size of website refresh, number/frequency of livestreams or videos, audience reach, or team size supported.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improve cross-channel publishing workflows, support a major website refresh, produce recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provide day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this as the launch/build phase if accurate.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; use more specific language like “standardized publishing” or “improved cross-channel coordination.”

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed as a foundation role, with clearer ownership and outcomes if any are available.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope + standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the digital/media work more direct and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications, including planning and developing supporting materials.”
- Elevate the podcast launch as the capstone: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable result: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or how the podcast supported advocacy/member engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production” language already covered in later NACo roles unless you specify this was the first podcast/multimedia initiative.
- Don’t overstate leadership here; later roles already show stronger team and platform ownership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it mixes software with capabilities and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. Tightening it to named tools only will make it cleaner and less repetitive.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia & Creative Software
- Replace with tool-focused list: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator
- If you want one capability phrase, keep only one concise add-on: Broadcast/livestream production
- Move “Podcast production” out of this skills item unless you can quantify it in experience; it reads more like a function than a tool
